title: The Apology — Sc144: solo close-up — Gumball nurses a hurt arm, screams, drops out of frame

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Solo close-up construction at its most economical: one puppet on one scene layer (GB) over a single locked background, and 51 frames carried almost entirely by the face-comp system. Gumball holds a gritted-teeth wince — eyes up, teeth clamped, rocking a hurt arm — for over 30 frames (head/mouth/eye comps: 1,112 kf vs the puppet's 655), and the release is punctuated in two steps: eyes slam shut at f39, a full open-mouth scream at f45, then he drops out of frame and the scene ends on the empty background. Pain, build and payoff are all face-comp poses; the body barely moves.
notes: Smallest file in the batch: 5 animated symbols and 1,995 total keyframes — one puppet, one background, one layer of performance (GB, 4 keyframe placements).
The background is a vector symbol ('Symbol 2'), not an LO_BG bitmap — the only scene in this batch without a bitmap plate — and it renders as a faint washed-out grey ceiling in the SWF export.
The wince is a hold, not a cycle: the gritted-teeth comp pose is sustained for ~38 frames with only small arm and eye changes before the scream releases it.
The scene ends on the empty plate (f51): the exit is a drop out of frame, not a cutaway.
